name: Hickam-Luzon Humanitarian Airdrop
precedent: Modeled on the doctrinal and geographic pattern of Operation Damayan (Nov 2013, Typhoon Haiyan relief) — this is a fictionalized scenario, not a re-creation of an actual classified mission.

route.stagingNote: En route staging/refuel point not modeled in v1.

timeline.description: Typhoon strikes Luzon; host-nation/embassy assistance request initiated.
USAID BHA validates the requirement for a unique DoD capability.
Request enters the Mission Tasking Matrix process to the Secretary of Defense.
INDOPACOM stands up a Joint Task Force.

PACAF theater AOC tasks the sortie via the ATO; DIRMOBFOR coordinates mobility flow. The AOC Weather Support Team begins fusing 17th Operational Weather Squadron theater forecasts into mission-specific weather products.

618 AOC/TACC tasks the specific tail number and crew from the 535th Airlift Squadron. The tasked Aircraft Commander receives a pre-flight Flight Weather Briefing (DD Form 175-1) from the Staff Weather Officer.

Sortie generated and mission executed via CDS bundle release over the drop zone — modeled as a state transition in v1, with no flight dynamics or drop-zone physics. Weather data continues to stream to both the AOC and the aircraft throughout, informing the Aircraft Commander's weather go/no-go decisions.

Aircraft returns to Hickam AFB and lands — modeled as a state transition, not a flown return leg. The same Aircraft Commander/ATC coordination and continuous JAAWIN-class weather monitoring from the outbound leg apply to the recovery, including the weather go/no-go decision's divert option.
Aircraft Commander leads the post-mission crew debrief, reporting execution results, any discrepancies, and mission outcome to the Mission Commander — the input the mission report is built from.
Mission report closes the loop back through the C2 chain.

doctrineSource.note: Air & Space Forces Magazine and Joint Force Quarterly coverage of the 2013 Typhoon Haiyan response, used as scenario precedent only — this record is a fictionalized scenario, not a report of a real mission.
